Next: set layer heights

Height by color

How the layers stack

  1. Check the base. The color covering the most area in the trace starts at the top. The smallest starts at the bottom, marked Base. Drag a different color to the bottom if you want it as the backing.
  2. Check which colors are raised. Put lettering or accents higher in the list when you want them to stand out. The maker extends each lower tier under the tiers above it so every raised area has material directly underneath. Lower colors can show on the sides of raised details.
  3. Set the top heights. Heights are measured from the print bed. For example, a 2 mm base, 4 mm middle tier, and 6 mm top tier print at 0–2, 2–4, and 4–6 mm. Dragging or using the arrow buttons reassigns the existing heights in the new order.

Build the plaque and rotate the 3D preview to check the stack before downloading.

Print without supports. A properly stacked plaque prints flat without supports. If the slicer shows areas that need supports, check that the base is flat on the bed and the tiers are aligned. Then review the layer order and rebuild if needed.

Trace your artwork, set the heights, then build the plaque.
